The Ranch That Wanted to Be a Colonial

BLOG POST #1

Why This Page Exists

Every house hunt has a moment where it stops being browsing and starts being a project. Ours was a ranch on Balsam Drive in Chelmsford — a perfectly ordinary single-storey house that we immediately wanted to turn into something it wasn't. Could the town even allow a second floor on top? What would that cost? And while we were at it: new doors everywhere, a full repaint, a new kitchen countertop.

So the house got investigated properly. Zoning first. Structure second. Then the money — the renovation priced out line by line, resale comps for a ~3,000 sq ft Chelmsford home checked, and the whole thing run twice: once with the second floor, once without. With it: roughly $1.28M all-in against a value of about $1.0–1.05M. Without it: about $732k in, roughly break-even. The dream floor was the thing that sank it.

A blog, because one spreadsheet wasn't enough

That investigation was too good to leave in a chat window. Every serious house deserves the same treatment — and a public verdict. So this page exists: a cooking-blog-style journal where each house is a recipe that either works or doesn't, stamped at the end — bought, or rejected, with the reason written on the stamp.

The rules of the kitchen

Every home, buy or lease, goes through the same routine. It gets its own post, and the post's background is that home's own street view or best view — rated by Parthey before anything is published. Eight standard questions get answered for every property before a verdict (they live under The Questions in the menu). Towns get their own filters as the hunt widens. And nothing here is decoration: if a number is on a post, it came from the investigation.

House #1 is already up — the ranch that wanted to be a colonial, rejected on the value maths. The shutter is open. Send the next listing.
